name: Miyapur Junction
desc: Ranked 6th most accident-prone locality in India (2024 national report). Heavy ORR merge traffic, unregulated U-turns, and high-speed two-wheelers make this Hyderabad's deadliest zone.

name: ORR 144.5 km
desc: Officially the deadliest single point on the Outer Ring Road. High-speed expressway merge with poor lighting and no pedestrian protection. Fatality cluster reported every quarter.
source: The Hindu / HMDA ORR Safety Audit 2025

name: ORR 14 km
desc: Consistent fatalities over five years at this expressway segment. Blind curve at high posted speed limit with merge from Patancheru industrial zone.

name: Rachakonda
desc: Complex multi-jurisdiction zone spanning Rachakonda commissionerate. Frequent heavy-vehicle vs two-wheeler collisions on the expressway shoulder.

name: Hayathnagar
desc: Part of the 12-km NH-65 corridor that recorded nearly 1,000 accidents in 2025 alone. High-speed highway cuts through dense residential and commercial access points.
source: Deccan Chronicle 2025 / The Hans India NH-65 Report

name: LB Nagar
desc: High-speed arterial NH-65 traffic meets a dense residential zone. Overspeeding, illegal U-turns, and pedestrian jaywalking contribute to frequent fatalities.

name: Abdullapurmet
desc: NH-65 corridor hotspot with uncontrolled access roads merging into the national highway. Trucks and buses cause frequent rear-end pile-ups.
source: The Hans India NH-65 Spot Report

name: Vanasthalipuram
desc: Dense colony road merges onto NH-65 without proper signals. High pedestrian exposure and mixed heavy-light vehicle conflict zone.

name: Hyderguda
desc: Central Zone's highest-risk intersection. Multi-directional traffic merge, no dedicated pedestrian crossing, and heavy autorickshaw congestion around the clock.
source: TSCTSL Central Zone Black Spot Report

name: Nampally
desc: Stretch identified as a Central Zone black spot. Narrow old-city road with heavy bus traffic, street vendors, and no footpaths forces pedestrians onto the carriageway.

name: Abids
desc: Old Gandhi Medical College area. Heavy commercial traffic, haphazard parking, and a complex circular junction with poor signal coordination.

name: Jubilee Hills
desc: High speeding-related mishap rate on wide residential roads. Late-night racing and drunk driving incidents concentrated here. Poor lighting on road dividers.
source: Times of India IT Corridor Accident Report 2024

name: Banjara Hills
desc: Near TV9 office and commercial stretch. Frequent accidents at Road No. 3 and 12 due to speeding, illegal parking blocking sight lines, and uncontrolled U-turns.
source: The Hindu GHMC-Traffic Police Joint Report

name: Madhapur
desc: Heavy 'tech lane' congestion with peak-hour gridlock and frequent minor-to-major collisions. Cab aggregator surge and wrong-way two-wheelers are primary hazards.
source: Times of India IT Corridor Report 2024

name: Gachibowli
desc: Tech corridor junction with DLF and Microsoft campus exits. Speeding on the flyover approach and sudden lane changes by IT commuters cause frequent collisions.
source: Times of India IT Corridor Report 2024

name: Yousufguda
desc: Narrow residential basti road intersects with a major arterial. Pedestrian–vehicle conflict is constant; no signal or guard present during peak school hours.

name: Marredpally
desc: North Zone black spot with heavy two-wheeler traffic and poorly timed signals. Frequent rear-end collisions on the main Marredpally road during morning rush.

name: Begumpet
desc: Near Parade Ground and HPS school. Heavy school-zone traffic mixes with airport approach vehicles. Pedestrian risk is extreme during school hours.
source: TSCTSL North Zone / Parade Ground Report

name: Madina
desc: South Zone black spot. Dense old-city intersection with competing religious procession traffic, TSRTC buses, and auto-rickshaws creating a perennial chokepoint.
source: TSCTSL South Zone Black Spot List

name: Puranapool
desc: Historic narrow gateway creates a severe bottleneck. Heavy goods vehicles attempt passage through under-height arches causing accidents and long traffic jams.
source: TSCTSL South Zone / Old City Report

name: Charminar
desc: Dense old-city roads with tourist overload, horse carts, and heavy trucks. Night bazaar traffic after 10 PM sees the highest accident rates in the old city.

name: Punjagutta
desc: One of Hyderabad's busiest junctions — heavy vehicle congestion, frequent signal violations, and multiple road merges at the flyover base make this extremely dangerous.

name: Kukatpally
desc: JNTU and KPHB corridors carry heavy IT-sector traffic. Night-time speeding and poor visibility near flyover underpasses are major risk factors.

name: Secunderabad Station
desc: Railway station traffic merge zone. Autos, cabs, and buses compete in a narrow corridor with no dedicated pedestrian lanes or zebra crossings.

name: Nagole
desc: ORR entry/exit ramp combined with local market traffic causes frequent rear-end collisions, especially during peak hours and after midnight.
